claims.text: A high-entropy alloy multilayer with a coherent interface can serve as a transition material between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
A coherent interface suppresses dislocation glide in an HEA multilayer.
A coherent interface promotes diffusion creep at high temperatures in an HEA multilayer.
The proposed material state is an HEA multilayer with a coherent interface.
The proposed intervention applies temperatures above 0.5Tm at a constant stress of 100 MPa.
Interface coherency is the structural mediator of the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
The coherent-interface HEA multilayer will exhibit a 30% increase in creep resistance relative to an incoherent-interface baseline.
Creep performance will be evaluated using creep strain rate in s^-1.
An HEA multilayer with an incoherent interface is the proposed baseline.
The proposed operating boundary is 0.5Tm to 0.8Tm and 50 MPa to 200 MPa.
The exact temperature and stress ranges for the creep-mechanism transition are uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if the coherent-interface multilayer's creep strain rate is not at least 20% lower than that of the incoherent-interface baseline at 0.6Tm and 100 MPa.
